title: Foot bed gap has no tolerance stack; the unstated zero foot-to-CR bond line can make the feet prop the tabs before the 22 joints are soldered
where: A.7 'Foot construction and bedding' (doc l.731-742), D.1 PM4 (2c)/(3) (l.1547), H.23(i) (l.2627-2628), T-A-06 pass criteria (l.2659), E feet row
fix:
1. Remove the unbudgeted pre-bond from the height chain. Change PM4 (2c) so that the foot is not cured to the CR before (3). Replacement wording: '(2c) (r7) Dry-fit FT1 and FT2 loose. Do not bond them before (3).' In (5) bed each foot on both faces in one operation, foot pressed up against the CR underside. Adopted sizing for this option: h_f = 2.54 - 0.30 - t_bond,nom. If the pre-bond is kept instead, state t_bond explicitly. Use a pressed thin film of t_bond <= 0.05 mm and set h_f = 2.54 - t_bed,nom - t_bond = 2.19 mm.

2. Add a tolerance budget to A.7 and H.23(i). Use the header body +-0.13 mm (TODO(verify: Samtec TSW drawing)), CR bow 0.118 mm local (IPC-6012 0.75 % x 15.72 mm), foot +-0.05 mm and bond 0-0.05 mm. The worst case is 0.35 mm, so a 0.30 mm nominal gap cannot guarantee clearance. Choose one of two options:
- Option (a): raise the nominal bed to 0.50 mm (h_f 2.04 mm, or 1.99 mm with a 0.05 mm bond), giving a worst-case minimum of 0.15 mm. Then re-run round4/calc/r7_calc.py H.23(i). The k_s values at t 0.50 mm are FT1 12.8-38.4 N/mm and FT2 32-96 N/mm (E A / t), and they change the pin-load and resonance rows.
- Option (b): keep 0.30 mm and add a measured gate.

3. Add a measured gate either way. Insert a step (3a) after seating and before soldering the 22 MB joints: 'With the CR seated and the props loose, check each foot spot. A 0.15 mm feeler passes under the foot, and a 0.45 mm feeler (0.65 mm under option a) does not pass. A 0.05 mm feeler does not pass under either header body at its column ends. If any check fails, remove the foot and correct h_f.' Add the same numeric gap criterion to T-A-06 item (8). Change the T-A-09 pass criterion to also require that the bed thickness measured at the lane or hole lies within the bed range.

4. Amend the T-A-06 pass text. Replacement wording: '>= 1.5 mm air between any CR bottom feature and MB copper (r7 exception: the FT1/FT2 foot beds, 0.30 +- 0.15 mm RTV on the 0.125 mm sheet over MB GND pour only, H.23(i))'.

Follow-on: regen of round4/calc/r7_calc.py H.23(i) if option (a) is taken. This is a doc/procedure fix with no firmware test, no pinmap-audit and no protocol-bump.

ADJACENT-FINDINGS: The H.23(i) pin-load and resonance figures assume t_bed 0.15-0.45 mm. Under an interference build, t_bed is 0, the foot becomes a rigid unbonded prop, and those rows do not apply. The 'nominal 0.30 mm' figure also appears in r7-2 (l.300) and the BOM feet row (l.1770) without the bond assumption.
claim: h_f = 2.54 - 0.30 = 2.24 mm assumes the foot sits directly on the CR underside, but PM4 (2c) bonds each foot to the CR with RTV before seating, and that bond line is taken as zero only in the calc (r7_calc_out.txt l.428: 'the foot-to-CR RTV bond is taken as zero thickness (ASSUMPTION; TODO(measure: T-A-09))'); the design doc states no bond thickness and no vertical tolerance. An uncontrolled RTV bond line of 0.05-0.2 mm, a header-body height tolerance (Samtec drawing not in the library), CR bow (IPC-6012 0.75 % over 47.3 mm = up to 0.35 mm, about 0.16 mm locally over the 15.7 mm from the 1x10 column to FT1) and foot machining tolerance together exceed the 0.30 mm nominal gap, so the claimed 0.15-0.45 mm bed range is not derived. In the interference case the bonded foot hard-props the tab at step (3): the CR cannot seat on the 1x10 column, and because FT1 sits at 1.63x and FT2 at 1.31x the column-to-column lever, a 0.10 mm interference at FT1 lifts the 1x10 body by about 0.06 mm while the 22 joints are soldered, preloading them. The 'feet take no preload' statement is then false. In addition, T-A-06 still requires '>= 1.5 mm air between any CR bottom feature and MB copper', which FT1/FT2 violate by design (0.30 mm bed + 0.125 mm sheet over the MB GND pour), and the r7 dry fit (T-A-06 item 8) has no gap criterion.
reason:
VERDICT: PARTIAL. The core defect is real. h_f = 2.24 mm leaves a 0.30 mm nominal gap only if the foot-to-CR RTV bond has zero thickness. That is a calc-only ASSUMPTION (r7_calc_out.txt l.428, r7_calc.py l.2564), and the design doc drops it at A.7 l.731-734, PM4 (2c) l.1547, H.23(i) l.2627 and the BOM feet row l.1770. No vertical tolerance budget exists anywhere: the doc has no bow statement and the library has no Samtec TSW drawing. The bonded foot is cured before step (3), so it is rigid while the CR is seated (PM4 (2c): 'Let the bond cure before (3)'). With interference, the foot lands on the sheet first. The CR then tilts about the far column and the header bodies lift by interference/lever (about 0.06 mm at the 1x10 column per 0.10 mm at FT1) while the 22 MB joints are soldered.

Overstated part: the 'preloads the joints' claim. Solder freezes the joints in the tilted geometry. With the props removed only gravity acts, so the residual joint preload is small. The real consequences are different. The header bodies no longer seat on the sheet, so the 'header bodies set the CR height' premise (A.7 l.733, PM4 (3)) is false. The intended RTV bed has zero thickness or cannot be formed, and the foot is an unbonded hard prop.

Why major: T-A-09 is the only foot check. Its criterion, 'the 0.05 mm feeler does not enter at either interface', passes when the foot sits directly on the sheet with no bed. It therefore passes while the claimed behaviour (a bonded 0.15-0.45 mm compliant bed) is absent. The 5 N pull may or may not reveal the missing bond, since the joints carry the pull. No pre-bed gap measurement exists: T-A-06 item (8) is a dry fit with no numeric gap criterion. The T-A-06 '>= 1.5 mm air between any CR bottom feature and MB copper' criterion is unamended stale text: FT1/FT2 sit 0.425 mm above MB copper by design. That part is minor doc drift on its own.

Source: authority 7-level design doc and its calc. The interference argument rests on standard tolerance figures (IPC-6012 bow; a recalled Samtec body tolerance, unverified because the drawing is not in references/).

Duplication: none known from the brief.

Exposure: no hardware-destruction path, so not critical. The defect is a build-geometry failure of a safety-relevant mechanical support (the tab-load relief computed in H.23(i)), with a gate that passes in the failure case.

title: The new W-lead band crosses C-D2/R171 (T2 joint), D-FC-EN with its EN bodge, C-D1 and SNS-FC; no rule protects these rework points, and PM3 now orients R171 into the band
where: A.3 r7 W-lead note (l.411), A.7 EVM reference placement (l.816-826), D.1 PM3 (l.1546), PM4 (6), H.23(l) (l.2635), T-A-08 MS3 (l.2662)
fix:
MINIMAL-FIX (doc-only; it triggers no test, pinmap-audit, protocol-bump, regen-coeffs or bench-incident follow-up):

(1) Append to the A.3 r7 W-lead note (l.411):

"In the W-lead band (MB top, y 68.30-98.044), every W lead leaves the tab X top edge at x <= 60.0; the H.23(l) routes leave at x 56.0. The leads are carried between the W5 fold and the chassis tie and bear on no MB part. No lead passes within 1.5 mm in plan of C-D2 and R171, D-FC-EN and its EN bodge resistor, or C-D1, with the W5 ribbon measured at its flat-cable edge. The leads cross SNS-FC and CSNS-FC only clear of their bodies."

Proof of the rule:
- The H.23(l) W3/W4/W5 route has centreline clearances of 6.23 mm (C-D1), 7.03 mm (D-FC-EN) and 9.20 mm (C-D2).
- The flat-ribbon edge clearances are 6.23 - 4.445 = 1.79 mm, 2.59 mm and 4.76 mm. All are at least 1.5 mm, so the route passes.
- The corner route (centreline 1.02-1.78 mm) fails the rule, which is the intent.

(2) Replace the PM3 r7 sentence with:

"r7: C-D2 pad 1 lies outside tab X (the C-D2 box is 3.64 mm from the FT1 body, H.23(i)). Fit R171 flat along C-D2, with its free end toward -x, and run the T2 wire from that end directly to F03. Neither R171 nor the T2 wire lies under the W-lead band route of A.3."

(3) In T-A-08, extend the MS3 scope to: "... inside each tab outline + 0.5 mm, under each foot spot, and in the W-lead band x 54-70, y 68.3-98.044 ...". Add the band to the chafe and strain inspection of T-F-12.

(4) Optionally, add the exit point (56.0, 68.30) to the l.824 text so that "29.98 mm from its corner" reads as the tie metric, not as the route.
claim: Every W lead leaves tab X and crosses the MB +y edge at x 56-68.91; W3, W4 and W5 run from the tab X corner (65.00, 68.30) to (68.75, 98.044). My .brd check finds six parts in the band x 54-70, y 68.3-98: C-D2 box x 67.12-70.04, y 68.80-70.90 (R171 rework on pad 1, T2 wire), D-FC-EN (RT1987) box x 67.15-70.52, y 71.57-76.07 (carries one of the 10 kOhm EN-to-GND bodge resistors named in MS3), C-D1 x 67.38-70.29, y 76.93-79.02, SNS-FC (INA253 FC) x 53.95-60.85, y 78.51-86.46, CSNS-FC and C4C-FC. The W5 flat cable alone is 14 x 0.635 = 8.89 mm wide; centred on the W3/W4/W5 line (x 65.2-66.0 at y 70-76) it spans about x 60.8-70.4 and lies on C-D2, R171 and D-FC-EN; the twisted 18 AWG pair (about 4 mm) reaches x 68.0 and overlaps D-FC-EN by about 0.8 mm. The route check tests only >= 10.10 mm from switched conductors, and the 'no named rework point covered' check applies only to the tabs. PM3 (r7) says 'orient R171 and the T2 wire away from tab X', that is toward +x/+y, directly under this bundle. The tie tension and vibration of 18/20 AWG leads then bear on a 0.1 % divider-top joint (T2 feeds H1 IN- and UVB) and on the EN pull-down bodge that keeps D-FC-EN off during MCU reset. MS3 surveys only the tab outlines + 0.5 mm and the foot spots, not this band.
reason:
The six parts in the band are real, and r7 indeed has no rule that keeps the W leads off MB parts or bodges between the tab X top edge (y 68.30) and the MB +y edge (y 98.044). MS3 also does not survey that band.

However, the finding's central geometry is wrong. It routes W3/W4/W5 from the tab X corner (65.00, 68.30) because doc l.411 and l.824 quote a tie distance measured from that corner. The H.23(l) calculation the doc cites leaves every W lead from (56.0, 68.30). On that route, the W5 ribbon laid flat clears C-D2/R171 by 4.76 mm, D-FC-EN by 2.59 mm and C-D1 by 1.79 mm. The claims "lies on C-D2, R171 and D-FC-EN" and "PM3 orients R171 directly under the bundle" therefore do not hold for the planned route.

Two parts of the finding hold:
- Every route passes over SNS-FC, and the W3/W4/W5 route passes over CSNS-FC.
- The text leaves the exit point free, so a corner dress (centreline 1.0-1.8 mm from C-D2, D-FC-EN and C-D1) is admitted.

PM3's instruction to orient the T2 wire away from tab X is self-contradictory, because T2 starts on tab X. With no computed strain or exposure path, severity caps at minor.

title: The USB corridor is the 7.62 mm receptacle silkscreen, not the plug overmold; the 4.97 mm W3/W4 channel and the reference placement rest on it, and MS2 does not measure the width
where: A.7 EVM reference placement and USB fallbacks (l.816-839), A.3 r7 note (l.424), H.23(l) (l.2634-2636), J.2 item 57, T-A-08 MS2
fix:

ADJACENT-FINDINGS:

- The corridor model is plan-view only. The plug elevation above the chassis (MB standoff + Teensy headers) against the chassis-level W3/W4 pair is not stated as an assumption.
claim: The corridor x 93.47-101.09 from y 93.73 is exactly the TEENSY41 package's layer-21 receptacle outline (93.47-101.09 x 88.01-93.73). A micro-B plug overmold is wider than the receptacle; a common overmold is about 10-11 mm wide (no drawing in the library). Centred at x 97.28, a 10.6 mm overmold occupies x 91.98-102.58, so the channel between the EVM right edge (x 88.50) and the corridor falls from 4.97 mm to about 3.5 mm, below the twisted 18 AWG silicone pair envelope (about 2 x 2.0 mm). MS2 measures only 'plug length and bend room'; with the width unmeasured, the reference placement can pass MS2 and still fail at assembly.
reason:
The finding's basis is real and its fix direction is correct. The corridor rectangle x 93.47-101.09 from y 93.73 is exactly the TEENSY41 layer-21 receptacle box: it is 7.62 mm wide, 5.715 mm deep and overhangs the Teensy outline by 1.27 mm. r7_calc.py uses it without widening, in both the 45 mm corridor and the open-ended corridor. The doc hedges the length (ASSUMPTION, MS2) but presents the width as fact, and MS2 (item 47) measures only plug length and bend room.

The reviewer's headline number assumes the overmold occupies the channel, and that is not established. The channel that matters is the 4.97 mm gap where the EVM wall exists, which is y >= 118.044. That is 24.31 mm past the receptacle face. Below that y the W3/W4 run is a diagonal at least 8 mm clear of any 10.6 mm overmold, so overmold width alone does not narrow the channel there. The 3.48 mm figure applies only if the overmold plus rigid boot is longer than about 24.3 mm, or if the cable bends toward -x within y 118-139.

Two more points are unverifiable from the repo. The 10.6 mm overmold width has no in-repo source. The plan-view analysis also ignores elevation: the plug sits at Teensy height on the MB, while the EVM and the pair are at chassis level.

Hence PARTIAL, severity minor. The reviewer's fix to inflate the corridor by overmold + 1 mm along the whole 45 mm (or open-ended) length is over-conservative. A 12.6 mm corridor would make the channel 2.48 mm and fail the reference placement on an envelope the cable does not occupy past the overmold. A stepped envelope is the correct model.

title: The chassis tie rule (<= 30 mm from the CR edge) passes only for a tie exactly on the MB edge line (margins 0.256 and 0.02 mm); any off-board chassis anchor fails T-F-12

fix:
MINIMAL-FIX (doc plus calc; no firmware): make the first anchor an adhesive tie base bonded on the MB solder mask, not a chassis tie at the edge line. Keep a chassis tie as a second, unconstrained anchor.

1. A.3 W1 row (l.398), replace the r7 parenthesis with: "(**r7:** an adhesive tie base, at most 10 x 10 mm, bonded on the MB solder mask with its centre at (62.0, 94.5) +- 1.5 mm, inside the part-free region x 56-69, y 91-98.04 of the MB; a chassis cable tie past the MB +y edge is the second anchor and is not distance-limited; H.23(l))".

3. Make the same change in A.7 l.823-825 and H.23(l) l.2634. Re-state l.2635 for fallback (i) using the same anchor.

4. r7_calc.py H.23(l): measure the tie distance to the anchor point with its tolerance box, not to P2 on the outline. Re-derive the route x2 cap from the part-free region instead of TIE_XMAX. Regenerate r7_calc_out.txt.

5. T-F-12 (l.2750): replace "the chassis tie at the MB +y edge (29.744 mm ...)" with "the MB tie base centre within 1.5 mm of (62.0, 94.5) (rule), its bundle grip <= 30 mm from the CR edge measured along the wire, and no base or bead over a part".

Alternative: restate the r5 30 mm rule with a measured or cited basis and an along-wire metric.

Follow-on skill: none of test/pinmap-audit/protocol-bump/regen-coeffs. It is a calc re-run (r7_calc.py H.23(l)) plus a doc revision.
claim: The tie is placed 'at the MB +y edge' (y 98.044): 29.744 mm from the tab X top edge (margin 0.256 mm) and 29.98 mm from the tab X corner for W3, W4 and W5 (margin 0.02 mm). A chassis tie must anchor off the board, past the edge; an adhesive tie base or chassis slot centred even 1-3 mm past y 98.044 gives 30.7-32.7 mm, so the reference build fails its own r5 strain-relief criterion in T-F-12. The route rule also clips the crossing to x <= 68.91 only to protect this margin.
reason:
VERDICT: CONFIRMED.

EVIDENCE:
- Doc l.398 (A.3 W1 row) puts the chassis tie "at the MB +y edge, 29.744 mm from the tab X top edge".
- Doc l.411 gives the margins of 0.256 mm and 0.02 mm, and caps the edge crossing at x <= 68.91 only to keep the tie within 30 mm.
- Doc l.823-825 (A.7) and l.2634 (H.23(l)) repeat the same distances.
- Doc l.2635 says fallback (i) "passes geometrically ... every chassis tie <= 30 mm", on the same tie model.
- T-F-12 (l.2750) keeps "chassis tie within 30 mm of the CR edge" as a check and puts the tie "at the MB +y edge (29.744 mm ...)".
- r7_calc.py:3137 computes the tie as the hypot from the tab X edge or corner to the edge-crossing point P2, which lies on y 98.0. That is a dimensionless point on the board outline, not a buildable anchor.
- r7_calc.py:3063 derives TIE_XMAX from that point.
- No tolerance is given anywhere.
- The doc's own A.7 (l.816) puts the EVM plate "on the chassis just past the MB +y edge", so any chassis anchor sits past y 98.044.

QUANTIFICATION: See the recomputed field. The tie point model gives 29.744 mm (margin 0.256 mm) and 29.9795 mm (margin 0.0205 mm). Any anchor with physical width, centred past the edge, fails: >= 30.99 mm for a 2.5 mm tie slot, 34.7-36.2 mm for a 10-13 mm adhesive base. My numbers match the reviewer's.

SOURCE:
- The MB .brd outline (authority 3/5 layout) and the r7_calc.py constants, recomputed by hand.
- The 30 mm criterion is the doc's own r5 rule (l.268, l.3159). The doc gives no measured basis for it.

DUPLICATION: None known. It overlaps the r5 finding cr-end-strain-relief-anchor, which set the 30 mm rule. This finding is about r7's placement against that rule, so it is not a duplicate.

SEVERITY-ASSESSMENT: Major. A published geometric pass verdict does not hold:
- H.23(l) states "every chassis tie <= 30 mm" for the reference placement and for fallback (i). The A.3 x <= 68.91 route clip rests on that verdict.
- A computed bound shows that every physically realizable chassis anchor exceeds 30 mm: at least 30.99 mm for a 2.5 mm tie slot.
- There is no hardware-destruction path. T-F-12 would catch the failure at inspection before Run, and the 30 mm rule is itself an unmeasured heuristic. That is why this is not critical.
- If the orchestrator weighs it as a buildability and doc defect caught by the test plan, minor is defensible.

ADJACENT-FINDINGS:
- The 30 mm rule has no stated physical basis (r5, l.268 and l.3159). Its plan-distance metric also ignores the 4.3 mm-plus vertical drop from the CR top to the chassis.
- Corridor fallback (i) (l.2635) inherits the same zero-extent tie model, so its "passes" verdict carries the same defect.

title: T-A-09's 5 N tab-tip pull loads the FT1 bed to up to 0.69 MPa (about 11x the 63.2 kPa service stress) through a load path that includes the sheet's deliberately peelable silicone PSA
where: T-A-09 (l.2663), D.1 PM4 (5) criterion, A.7 'Foot removal and bond fallback' (l.743-747), H.23(i) (l.2628), J.2 item 55
fix:
MINIMAL-FIX (documentation and test spec only; follow-on skill: test, a T-A-09 text revision; no firmware or coefficient regeneration):

(1) T-A-09 'how' column: replace 'then a 5 N upward pull at each tab tip for 10 s (spring scale)' with 'then a 2 N upward pull at the tab X tip (65.00, 62.30) for 10 s (spring scale, wire loop under the tab X -x/+x edges; 2 N loads the FT1 bed with 0.48-1.76 N, >= 1.19x the 0.404 N 30 g service bound at every k_s 14-128 N/mm, H.23(i)); at tab Y, a 2 N pull through a loop entered from the tab side (x), never past the +y edge (L-FC 0.862 mm, H.23(b))'.
   Proof: FT1 share 0.241-0.879 (r7_calc_out.txt), so 2 N x 0.241 = 0.482 N, which exceeds 63.2 kPa x 6.40 mm2 = 0.404 N.
   If the operator prefers a larger margin, keep 5 N but state why (handling proof, 3-11x service) and accept the PSA risk explicitly.

(2) T-A-09 pass criteria: add 'and the 0.05 mm feeler does not enter between the polyimide sheet and the MB solder mask within 3 mm of either foot'.
   T-A-09 fail column: add 'a sheet-to-mask lift is a PSA failure, not an RTV failure; re-press the sheet and repeat before invoking the mask-bond fallback'.

(3) J.2 item 55: append 'The pull load path also crosses the sheet's silicone PSA to the MB mask (the A.7 removal layer); its flatwise strength is TODO(verify: polyimide tape datasheet). Optional coupon before the vehicle build: an RTV bed on the chosen sheet on an MB-mask coupon (a spare MB or any FR-4 with LPI mask), pulled to failure, recording which interface fails.'

ADJACENT-FINDINGS: none.
claim: From the calc, a 10 N tab X tip push puts 2.41-8.79 N on FT1 (k_s 14-128 N/mm); the 5 N proof pull therefore puts 1.2-4.4 N in tension on its 6.40 mm2 bed, 0.19-0.69 MPa, against the stated service bound of <= 63.2 kPa at 30 g (3-11x). The tension path is foot -> RTV -> polyimide -> silicone PSA -> MB solder mask, and A.7 defines the sheet as the sacrificial layer that is removed by peeling, so the PSA is the intended weak link; J.2 item 55 tracks only RTV-to-polyimide adhesion. A typical silicone-PSA polyimide tape peels at about 0.2-0.4 N/mm (estimate, no datasheet in the library); over the 11.2 mm FT1 perimeter that is about 2-4.5 N, the same order as the test load. The test can therefore lift the sheet and fail a bed that is adequate for service, or pass only by straining the PSA. In addition, a hook under the tab Y tip has no room: the tab Y +y edge is 0.862 mm from the L-FC body.
reason:
VERDICT: PARTIAL.

EVIDENCE:
- A.7, design l.743-747: the polyimide sheet is the sacrificial layer. Removal means cutting the bed and peeling the sheet, and the MB mask is never bonded in the baseline.

claim: FT1 is bedded from one long face: the RTV must flow 1.6 mm under the foot into a 0.30 mm gap. FT2 is filled through a 1.0 mm hole about 3.9 mm long (1.6 mm CR + 2.24 mm foot). reason:
The finding is partly confirmed. The defect is a missing rationale, not a wrong number or an unsafe default.

- Every load figure the reviewer quotes matches r7_calc_out.txt l.446-454 and the doc text (l.753-754, H.23(i) l.2628).
- The design document never says why the feet are fitted by default. 0.3 r7-2 and A.7 l.715 assert "fitted by default", and H.23(i) lists the pin loads with and without the feet.

1. The claim that "the only remaining argument is modal or damping" does not hold for FT1. Severity is minor. No published number is wrong, and both choices are mechanically benign: a 30 g pin load of 0.17-0.32 N in either case, and bed stress <= 63 kPa. No exposure path leads to hardware damage. This is doc drift: a design decision stated without its rationale, with the decision rule in J.2 item 50 pointing one way only.
